newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk IDC targets $200 mln 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turk IDC targets $200 mln 1997 sales.

text.p: Turkish steel ingots and rolled products producer Izmir Demir Celik Sanayi A.S. targets to increase its total sales to more than $200 million in 1997, from $190 million in 1996, a senior company official said.

"Depending on the production capacity increase in late 1996, we will raise the turnover to over $200 million in 1997 from $190 million in 1996," Servet Erocal, vice president of the company, told Reuters in an interview.
The company exports about 80 percent of its total output.
Izmir Demir Celik shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange closed at 2,125 lira on Monday, up from Friday's 2,100.

Izmir Demir Celik which mainly produces reinforcing and plain steel bars used in building and infrastructure constructions, newly expanded its annual hot milling capacity to 650,000 tonnes from 600,000 tonnes.
It uses scrap iron to produce steel ingots as raw material for the main rolled steel products.

The company raised its rolled products output to 581,000 tonnes in 1996 from 477,000 tonnes a year ago and set the 1997 target at 630,000 tonnes. Production of steel ingots rose to 689,000 tonnes last year from 617,000 tonnes in 1995 and is targeted at 728,000 tonnes for this year.
Erocal said the company's production capacity would be fully used in 1997, same as in 1996, but added that no capacity expansions were planned for this year.

"We will have 650,000 tonnes of output in 1997 from 728,000 tonnes of steel ingots. 630,000 tonnes of the final output will be standard quality and the rest will be sold as sub-standard products," he added.
The company transports most of its exports by its own vessels after buying a second 41,500-dwt bulk cargo ship last year for $15 million.
"We have 1.2 million tonnes of annual sea-cargo capacity, 500,000 tonnes of exports and 700,000 tonnes of raw-material imports," Erocal said.

He said the company sold this year's first four-month output by mid-February and is receiving orders for the following three months. Raw-materials needed for the pre-sold production are in stocks, Erocal said.

Turkey has around 10 million tonnes of total rolled steel production capacity, far above the domestic demand estimated at 3.0 to 3.5 million tonnes. Therefore, most Turkish hot mills which operate with electric-fired furnaces, export their output.
"Turkish mills control 35 to 40 percent of the world exports in rolled steel products," Erocal said.
On the other hand, Turkey is one of the biggest importers of scrap iron used by the these mills as the main raw material.
"Turkish steel sector affects world scrap iron prices because producers act in solidarity. But there is no solidarity in exporting," he added.
The main shareholder of the company is T. Is Bankasi, Turkey's leading private bank, with 55.34 percent stake.
